segments.arabic: [1030] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن عاصم وحصين عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from ‘Asim and Husayn, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: أقام النبي ﷺ تسعة عشر يقصر فنحن إذا سافرنا تسعة عشر قصرنا وإن زدنا أتممنا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed for nineteen days, shortening the prayer. When we travelled for nineteen days, we shortened the prayer; if we exceeded that, we prayed it in full.

notes: Both occurrences located. Nineteen is repeated in the selected text. Historical print adds an explicit day word and residence phrase; the selected and modern wording is shorter. No travel ruling is inferred.

Days supplies the understood unit after nineteen in English; the selected Arabic leaves the unit unstated. The historical print explicitly has days and adds a residence phrase. No place of residence, number of shortened rak‘ahs or legal duration rule is supplied.

segments.arabic: [1031] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي إسحاق قال:
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: سمعت أنسا يقول خرجنا مع النبي ﷺ من المدينة إلى مكة فكان يصلي ركعتين ركعتين حتى رجعنا إلى المدينة قلت: أقمتم بمكة شيئا قال أقمنا بها عشرا
segments.english: I heard Anas say, “We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from Medina to Mecca. He prayed two rak‘ahs at a time until we returned to Medina.” I asked, “Did you stay in Mecca for any time?” He said, “We stayed there for ten days.”

notes: The complete route and the question about the stay in Makkah are present; ten remains distinct from nineteen in the preceding report.

The I heard Anas introduction stays visible with the account, so its following first-person question is not detached from the narrator framing. Two rak‘ahs at a time retains the Arabic repetition. Days supplies the understood unit after ten. The old web-typo finding was caused by tag-to-space extraction; the actual inline HTML renders two.

segments.arabic: [1032] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: أخبرني نافع عن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi‘ informed me, from ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت مع النبي ﷺ بمنى ركعتين وأبي بكر وعمر ومع عثمان صدرا من إمارته ثم أتمها
segments.english: I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and with Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, and with ‘Uthman in the early part of his rule. Then he prayed it in full.

notes: The successive Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and early Uthman references remain together. Later completion of prayer is not omitted.
The selected chain names Abdullah without ibn Umar. Do not expand that name from a different witness. The Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and early Uthman clauses remain together.

segments.arabic: [1033] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة أنبأنا أبو إسحاق قال: سمعت حارثة بن وهب قال
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. Abu Ishaq informed us. He said: I heard Harithah ibn Wahb say:

segments.arabic: صلى بنا النبي ﷺ آمن ما كان بمنى ركعتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in two rak‘ahs at Mina at a time of the greatest security.

checkedBody: The Prophet I led us in the prayer at Mina during the peace period by offering two Rakat.
comparisons.note: Stray English character appears after the Prophet label.

notes: The Mina report retains the security wording and its separate Harithah route. This occurrence is not deduplicated with the adjacent Mina reports.
Greatest security retains the superlative force of آمن; Ibn Hajar explicitly discusses that form. No participant count or a new legal explanation is imported.

segments.arabic: [1034] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد عن الأعمش قال: حدثنا إبراهيم قال: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن يزيد يقول
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us, from al-A‘mash, who said: Ibrahim related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid say:

segments.arabic: صلى بنا عثمان بن عفان رضى الله تعالى عنه بمنى أربع ركعات فقيل ذلك لعبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله تعالى عنه فاسترجع، ثم قال صليت مع رسول الله ﷺ بمنى ركعتين وصليت مع أبي بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه بمنى ركعتين وصليت مع عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه بمنى ركعتين فليت حظي من أربع ركعات ركعتان متقبلتان
segments.english: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, led us in four rak‘ahs at Mina. ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was told of this, and he uttered the declaration of return to Allah. Then he said, “I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, and I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. Would that my share of four rak‘ahs were two accepted rak‘ahs.”

notes: The complete Ibn Masud reaction and his concluding wish are retained. The full route and each repeated two-unit statement require individual translation.

The selected verb استرجع is rendered as uttered the declaration of return to Allah; a complete Quran quotation and an added emotional description are not supplied. All four companion honorific occurrences and all three separate Mina/two-rakah phrases remain.

segments.arabic: [1035] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا وهيب قال: حدثنا أيوب عن أبي العالية البراء عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu al-‘Aliyah al-Barra’, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: قدم النبي ﷺ وأصحابه لصبح رابعة يلبون بالحج فأمرهم أن يجعلوها عمرة إلا من معه الهدي
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his companions arrived on the morning of the fourth, reciting the talbiyah for Hajj. He ordered them to make it an ‘Umrah, except those who had the sacrificial animals with them.

segments.arabic: تابعه عطاء عن جابر
segments.english: ‘Ata’ corroborated it from Jabir.

comparisons.note: The closing corroboration is abridged and does not name Ata.

checkedBody: The Prophet and his companions reached Mecca in the morning of the 4th Dhul-Hijja reciting Talbiya (O Allah! We are obedient to your orders, we respond 4 to your call) . . . intending to perform Hajj. The Prophet ordered his companions to assume the lhram for Umra instead of Hajj, excepting those who had Hadi (sacrifice) with them.
comparisons.note: Extraneous numeral occurs inside the parenthetical talbiyah explanation.

notes: The fourth-morning report ends with Ata from Jabir corroboration; this is part of the selected report rather than a chapter note.

segments.arabic: [1036] حدثنا إسحاق بن إبراهيم الحنظلي قال: قلت لأبي أسامة حدثكم عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali related to us. He said: I said to Abu Usamah: ‘Ubayd Allah related to you, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: لا تسافر المرأة ثلاثة أيام إلا مع ذي محرم
segments.english: A woman must not travel for three days except with a mahram.

checkedBody: The Prophet said, "A woman should not travel for more than three days except with a Dhi-Mahram (i.e. a male with whom she cannot marry at all, e.g. her brother, father, grandfather, etc.) or her own husband.)"
comparisons.note: Adds a more-than qualification not present in the selected three-day wording.

notes: The first travel report includes Ishaq addressing Abu Usamah. The Arabic specifies three days without the added more-than qualification in the Khan comparison.

The chain retains Ishaq addressing Abu Usamah with related to you. No response by Abu Usamah is invented. The Arabic specifies three days, without more than, and mahram remains a transliterated technical term rather than an added list of relatives.

segments.arabic: [1038] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب قال: حدثنا سعيد المقبري عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us. He said: Sa‘id al-Maqburi related to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: لا يحل لامرأة تؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن تسافر مسيرة يوم وليلة ليس معها حرمة
segments.english: It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel a journey of a day and a night without a mahram with her.

segments.arabic: تابعه يحيى بن أبي كثير وسهيل ومالك عن المقبري عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Suhayl and Malik corroborated it from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

comparisons.note: The closing note names Malik but omits the other two selected corroborators.

checkedBody: The Prophet (p.b.u.h) said, "It is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel for one day and night except with a Mahram."

notes: The one-day-and-night report and all three closing corroborating transmitters remain. Do not silently substitute a commentary definition for the selected term.

Mahram is the provisional lexical rendering of حرمة, matching the gloss in Ibn Hajar and the two English comparisons. This is a term check, not a new definition or ruling. All three closing corroborators and the final Abu Hurayrah honorific remain.

segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir and Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت الظهر مع النبي ﷺ بالمدينة أربعا والعصر بذي الحليفة ركعتين
segments.english: I prayed Dhuhr with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Medina as four rak‘ahs, and ‘Asr at Dhu al-Hulayfah as two rak‘ahs.

comparisons.note: The explicit Asr prayer name is absent from this English body.

checkedBody: offered four Rakat of Zuhr prayer with the Prophet (p.b.u.h) at Medina and two Rakat at Dhul-Hulaifa. (i.e. shortened the 'Asr prayer).
comparisons.note: The opening first-person pronoun is missing; Asr is supplied parenthetically.

notes: Both reports located, but the modern printed main text lacks the explicit Asr name found in the selected source and the historical print. Both readings are recorded.

segments.arabic: [1040] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا سفيان عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: الصلاة أول ما فرضت ركعتين فأقرت صلاة السفر وأتمت صلاة الحضر
segments.english: When prayer was first prescribed, it was two rak‘ahs. The prayer of travel was left as it was, and the prayer of residence was made complete.

segments.arabic: قال الزهري فقلت لعروة ما بال عائشة تتم قال تأولت ما تأول عثمان
segments.english: Al-Zuhri said: I asked ‘Urwah, “Why does ‘A’ishah pray in full?” He said, “She adopted the interpretation that ‘Uthman adopted.”

notes: The Aishah report includes the subsequent al-Zuhri/Urwah exchange. Interpretation is attributed to that exchange and must not be replaced by a new explanation.

The final al-Zuhri/Urwah exchange is a separate narrator note. Adopted the interpretation renders تأولت rather than replacing it with merely did the same. The draft does not supply the substance of that interpretation.

segments.arabic: [1041] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سالم عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ إذا أعجله السير في السفر يؤخر المغرب حتى يجمع بينها وبين العشاء قال سالم وكان عبد الله يفعله إذا أعجله السير
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste on a journey, delay Maghrib until he combined it with ‘Isha’. Salim said: ‘Abdullah used to do this when travelling in haste.

segments.arabic: وزاد الليث قال: حدثني يونس عن ابن شهاب قال سالم
segments.english: Al-Layth added. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab. Salim said:

segments.arabic: كان ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما يجمع بين المغرب والعشاء بالمزدلفة
segments.english: Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, used to combine Maghrib and ‘Isha’ at Muzdalifah.

segments.arabic: قال سالم وأخر بن عمر المغرب وكان استصرخ على امرأته صفية بنت أبي عبيد فقلت له الصلاة، فقال سر فقلت: الصلاة، فقال سر حتى سار ميلين أو ثلاثة ثم نزل فصلى، ثم قال هكذا رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي إذا أعجله السير،
segments.english: Salim said: Ibn ‘Umar delayed Maghrib when he had been urgently called to help concerning his wife, Safiyyah bint Abi ‘Ubayd. I said to him, “The prayer!” He said, “Go on.” I said, “The prayer!” He said, “Go on,” until he had travelled two or three miles. Then he dismounted and prayed. Then he said, “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray when travelling in haste.”

segments.arabic: وقال عبد الله رأيت النبي ﷺ إذا أعجله السير يؤخر المغرب فيصليها ثلاثا ثم يسلم ثم قلما يلبث حتى يقيم العشاء فيصليها ركعتين ثم يسلم ولا يسبح بعد العشاء حتى يقوم من جوف الليل
segments.english: ‘Abdullah said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste, delay Maghrib and pray it as three rak‘ahs, then say the taslim. Then he would wait only a little before saying the iqamah for ‘Isha’, praying it as two rak‘ahs, and saying the taslim. He would not pray voluntary prayers after ‘Isha’ until he rose during the middle of the night.

comparisons.note: A death-or-dying gloss for Safiyyah must not replace the selected alarm wording or its uncertainty.

checkedBody: "I saw Allah's Apostle delaying the Maghrib prayer till he offered it along with the 'Isha' prayer whenever he was in a hurry during the journey." Salim narrated, "Ibn 'Umar used to do the same whenever he was in a hurry during the journey." And Salim added, "Ibn 'Umar used to pray the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers together in Al-Muzdalifa." Salim said, "Ibn 'Umar delayed the Maghrib prayer because at that time he heard the news of the death of his wife Safiya bint Abi 'Ubaid. I said to him, 'The prayer (is due).' He said, 'Go on.' Again I said, 'The prayer (is due).' He said, 'Go on,' till we covered two or three miles. Then he got down, prayed and said, 'I saw the Prophet praying in this way, whenever he was in a hurry during the journey.' 'Abdullah (bin 'Umar) added, "Whenever the Prophet was in a hurry, he used to delay the Maghrib prayer and then offer three Rakat (of the Maghrib) and perform Taslim, and after waiting for a short while, Iqama used to be pronounced for the 'Isha' prayer when he would offer two Rakat and perform Taslim. He would never offer any optional prayer till the middle of the night (when he used to pray the Tahajjud)."
